summary: Registered the successor execution that closes the last unexercised consequence. The harness's new lost_entry_discard case collapses a five-voter committed configuration to one voter, snapshots it, makes it five voters again, stops everything, lets the former leader restart, acknowledge one uniquely named commit on a single copy and be stopped, then brings the four voters back with the flag disabled, has a majority elect without the payload, stops that leader so the remaining three elect once more in a strictly higher term, and only then rebuilds the holder and scans every store for the payload. Local verification before submission: with the flag enabled the acknowledged payload was absent from every store after the holder rejoined (copies_after_rejoin 0, discarded true, holder last index 117 after the rejoin versus the payload's own index), so an acknowledged commit was discarded once a majority that never held it formed higher-term leadership; with the flag disabled nothing was acknowledged at all ("node is not the leader"). Three comparisons are declared — durability on a majority of the committed configuration, the discard itself, and the acknowledgement control — and validation reports a valid update with one experiment created and an execution requested. Incomplete: the receipt is outstanding, so this turn recorded no interpretation; the earlier finding that the three-voter variant does not discard its entry remains as the in-run contrast that motivated the extra election step.
